references.text: The parallel text in [ref:Matt 6:25|Matthew 6:25] is almost identical: "Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear." In both places, Jesus conveys the same teaching about not worrying.

[ref:Sal 55:23|Psalm 55:22]: "Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you." This is a foundational Old Testament text about entrusting one's worries to God, which Jesus expands upon in his teaching here.

[ref:Fil 4:6-7|Philippians 4:6–7]: "Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God." Paul gives the same exhortation as Jesus: do not worry, but trust in God.
[ref:1 Pet 5:7|1 Peter 5:7]: "Cast all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you." Peter builds upon the same tradition from Jesus about casting one's worries onto God.

[ref:Luk 12:29-31|Luke 12:29–31]: Jesus summarizes the teaching that begins in verse 22 by saying that the disciples should not anxiously ask what they will eat and drink, but seek God's kingdom. The verse expands on this same theme.
[ref:1 Tim 6:8|1 Timothy 6:8]: "But if we have food and clothing, with these we shall be content." Paul reflects Jesus' teaching that food and clothing should not be the object of anxious worry.

[ref:Matt 6:31-33|Matthew 6:31–33]: "Therefore do not be anxious, saying, 'What shall we eat?' … But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness." This parallel passage shows that worry about earthly things should be replaced with trust in God's care.
[ref:Sal 37:5|Psalm 37:5]: "Commit your way to the Lord; trust in him, and he will act." The Old Testament background for Jesus' exhortation not to worry but to trust in God's providence.

[ref:Hebr 13:5-6|Hebrews 13:5–6]: "Keep your life free from love of money … for he has said, 'I will never leave you nor forsake you.'" The exhortation against materialism and worry, grounded in God's faithfulness.
